coverage.r1: Whole file read in order. Several Amal lines are ASR-garbled (12:13 بدائية = likely ورديّة; 13:42 فعلاً = likely فعلين; 38:33 أشياءي نوع الإل unreadable, so the 38:30 كل أشيائي exchange is not scored; 42:15 صحته; 51:36 سائل; 55:33 أنا واعي; 56:15 عيني ليه؟). Medi garbles not scored: 07:32 الليلة جو كتير كتير (meaning unclear), 30:02 ببي / 30:21 كيك؟ (window sentence, unreadable), 39:59 أكره كاسته, 54:24 إمّني, 55:05 أبن كتير, 55:30 بفيت, 56:04 بفزت (= ببسّط, accepted by Amal), 57:14 بزور. S4 pronunciation left out: 03:11 جهزت/جهّزت shadda (F3), 07:46 قربان for خربان, 15:02 أزعشتك (ج/ش), 25:08 بيتايو (dropped ق), 27:05 بعيم for بقيم, 30:49 albo, 33:41 سهون/سهوني for صحوني, 43:04-43:16 انكسرت letter-order slip she flagged as 'letters order', 52:52 اشي/إشي vowel. 03:38-05:51, 17:06-18:06, 46:08-48:13, 57:37-1:02:33 are mostly English discussion (recording protocol, verb-pair choice, causative verbs). Latin-transliterated stretch 06:38-07:20 (date and clock). 54:40 'شو الـ verbs اليوم' echoes Amal's own English term 'unverbs' one line earlier, so not tier 3. 'air conditioning', 'bones', 'YouTube' are not on her sheet, so his English there is not tier 3. Metathesis slips (02:59 زعمت, 27:50 بخسر, 34:14 يسكر) are written as low/medium vocab rows because Amal voiced each fix and each produces a different real word; the settler may rule them S4.
coverage.r2: Whole file read. Holes/garbles: 06:38-07:20 date and clock are Latin-transliterated (tisa asha, Sa alaat ila tult, Intayn); 12:13 Amal's colour fix is garbled (بدائية); 24:05-24:38 the root قصد is transcribed as أزد/أزت/مهم; 24:50-25:16 بتداي/بيتايوكي = بيدايقوكي with ق dropped; 26:49-27:05 بعين/بعيم = بقيم (S4); 30:21 كيك؟ and 39:59 أكره كاسته are unreadable; 38:33 Amal 'أشياءي نوع الإل' unreadable (no row); 42:00-42:15 hand/إيد exchange garbled (Dan's, eat, ear); 42:15-42:29 Medi talks to a passer-by in English; 51:36 Amal 'سائل' and 55:30-55:33 'بفيت'/'أنا واعي' unreadable; 55:05 'أبن كتير' and 56:04 'بفزت' garbled. Not filed as errors: S4 sound slips (03:11 جهزت/جهّزت shadda, 15:02 أزعشتك, 29:46 سكرتي self-fixed, 32:58/33:11 بتزلي for بتضلي, 33:41 سهوني for صحوني, 43:10 'letters order' on انكسرت, 44:18 اثنعش, 52:52 اشي/إشي vowel); 05:58 الأربعاء→الخميس self-fixed before Amal's لا; 16:39 and 25:38 'كم مرة؟' were listening misunderstandings (هديك المرة / الفعل الجاي), not filed; 22:24 'تكوني or مبسوطة?' and 43:32 'كان عمرها أو عمرها كان؟' and 36:58 past of بنكسر were grammar questions he asked before erring, not filed; 51:20 'bones' he never attempted and Amal did not supply, not filed. 'air conditioning' (12:53, 53:14, 53:29) is not on her sheet and Amal herself said الـ air conditioning تبعي, so no tier-3 row. Long stretches 03:40-05:52, 17:06-18:06, 46:08-48:13, 57:27-1:02:33 are English discussion.

r3_note: Pass 2. The compare step mis-paired D9/D10: r1-28 (متأكتي, 20:57) was paired with r2-34 (إلي→إنو, 21:01) while r1-29 is the same إلي→إنو row - so إلي→إنو was in fact found by BOTH readers; it is settled once under D10 (high) and D9 carries only the متأكتي piece. D22 is kept but re-labelled: the transcript shows a wrong VERB (صلح for ساعد, he fixed to ساعدني after her prompt at 11:02), not a D3 preposition-ending error - the merger should check whether an agreed row already covers 10:34 صلاحني→ساعدني and dedupe. One added row (53:14 تعبي→تبعي) may also duplicate an agreed row; match by t and wrong. Lesson-wide: ASR badly garbles his Arabic in this file (Next far, take Allah, Dan's, بتداي), so several B rows are low; his D1-style letter swaps (زعمت/عزمت, تعبي/تبعي) are ruled tier-1 vocab because they produce a different real word that Amal treated as wrong, not as a slip.

rows.medi_said: كيف كان الـ-- كيف كان العروسة؟ عروس؟
rows.why: He asked how the wedding was but said عروسة/عروس (bride); she supplied عرس (wedding); he repeated عروس again at 01:57 and she let that pass.

He said زعمت (I claimed) three times in a row (02:49, 02:56, 02:59) for عزمت (I invited; sheet: i invited | Ana 3azamet | أنا عزمت); Amal first made him retry (جرّب كم مرة) then recast عزمت, and he himself flags it as a corrected word at 04:05 - a consistent different real word, not a one-off S4 slip, so tier 1 not tier 2.
rows.r3_why: Both readers agree on the slip; tier 1 fits: زعم is a different lexical item, not a wrong form of عزم, and she treated it as an error (retry prompt then recast).

rows.amal_said: I just did it. I just repeated what you said. ألفين ستة وعشرين.
rows.why: Date: he stopped at ألفين (2000) and dropped ستة وعشرين; she supplied the full year ألفين ستة وعشرين; she also confirmed day-first order عشرة تسعة at 06:46.

rows.medi_said: Sa alaat ila nun-- ila tult.
rows.why: Clock time: he said الساعة تلات (three) for 2:40; she prompted 'three or two?', he fixed to Intayn, she recast تنتين إلا تلت (07:22).
'A video on YouTube' takes على, he used لـ (for/of); she let it pass; YouTube itself is not on her sheet so the English word is not an error.
rows.english: I watched a video on YouTube.

rows.why: Her sheet fixes the preposition on this verb (i call | Ana barenn (3ala) | أنا برن); he used لـ; she let it pass while they hunted the word for electrician (08:39-09:10); low because رنّ لـ is also heard colloquially and she did not react.
rows.r3_why: Real per her own sheet (3ala), unflagged by Amal, so grammar-B low; not a duplicate.

rows.medi_said: Is it raki? What was electricity?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for 'electricity' and she supplied كهربا (sheet: electricity | Kahraba | كهربا).

rows.medi_said: مهندس-- Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟
rows.why: Profession idafa: el- goes on the second noun (مهندس الكهربا); he put none; she recast and he repeated it right at 09:07.

rows.medi_said: كراجي. This is a new word. It's not gonna be on the list.
rows.why: Amal volunteered كهربجي at 09:10; he said it right once (09:13) then reproduced it as كراجي (garage-man, a different word) at 09:30, 09:39 and 09:48, and she recast كهـ، كهربجي syllable by syllable at 09:42 - he attempted the word and got it wrong, so a recast fix (tier 1), not a didn't-know; low stakes because the word was 30 s old and not on her sheet.
rows.r3_why: Tier 0 is for a word he never attempted or asked for; here he produced a wrong word and she recast it, so tier 1 recast.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- uh, كهربجي، هو مهندس
rows.right: مش (هو مش كهربجي، هو مهندس) (my reading)
rows.why: Negating a noun in the plain present takes مش, not ما يكون (no 'to be' in the present); she let it pass.
rows.english: He is not an electrician, he is an engineer.

rows.medi_said: صلاح، صلاحني شوي. / صلاحلي, helps to me, شوي.
rows.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me?
rows.why: He used صلح (fix) to mean 'helped me'; she explained صلحني = he fixed me, صلح لي = fixed for me, then asked if he meant helped; he produced ساعدني and she confirmed (11:10); sheet: help | Saa3ed | ساعد.

rows.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me?
rows.why: He meant 'he helped me a bit' (10:40 'helps to me') but used the verb صلح (fix) - a different word; Amal explained صلحني = he fixed me, then prompted 'did you wanna say he helped me?' and he fixed to ساعدني (11:07, 'Oops'); the D3 reading (صلح لي vs صلحني) is moot because the -ني object is right for his intended verb ساعد.
rows.r3_why: Real fix she voiced, but the transcript supports a wrong-verb vocab row (صلح for ساعد), not the D3 preposition-ending row r2 wrote; merger should dedupe against any agreed 10:34 row.

rows.medi_said: بلوزة، um, ورداني لـ أول مرة برأيك
rows.amal_said: بدائية. (ASR; likely ورديّة) / صح لأول مرة.
rows.right: وردنية (his fixed form she approved with صح at 12:16)
rows.why: بلوزة is feminine so the colour adjective needs the feminine ending; he said masculine ورداني, she recast (her line is garbled) and approved his وردنية; her sheet word for pink is زهري.
rows.english: A pink blouse, for the first time.

rows.why: Wrong form of a verb he knows (sheet: i stayed/kept | Ana dallait | أنا ضليت); she did not understand and supplied ضليت; he said دولت again at 12:41; could be argued S4 (ض/د) but the vowel shape is also wrong.

rows.medi_said: اه، this is take Allah بيتي.
rows.why: Telling her he stayed home (ضليت, ASR 'دولت'/'take Allah') he said بيتي with no preposition; she prompted 'بِ أو فِي بيتي؟' and he fixed to بي بيتي at 12:50; medium because his line is ASR-garbled.
rows.r3_why: Transcript shows the prompt and his fix; real grammar row only r1 wrote.

rows.right: عشان الـ air conditioning كان (خربان) / عشان في (my reading)
rows.why: Reason for staying home was the broken AC he described at 07:46 and again at 53:29 (عشان الـ air conditioning كان خربان); يكون (subjunctive 'be') has no place here - either في (there is) or كان (was); Amal moved on to شو بتتذكر; low because the clause was left unfinished; 'air conditioning' is not on her sheet so no tier-3.
rows.r3_why: Wrong ykoon in a plain statement, unflagged; kept low because the sentence is a fragment.

rows.why: 'One word' puts the number/adjective after the noun; he fronted it (English order); she recast كلمة وحدة and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
rows.why: 'Two verbs' needs the dual فعلين, he said فعل + تنين; her reply is transcribed 'بس فعلاً', which is not a fix as written - it may be an ASR-garbled 'بس فعلين' (same 'بس X' recast shape as her 'بس كلمة وحدة' 2 s earlier) but the transcript cannot prove it, so B for Amal to confirm.
rows.r3_why: Both saw the slip; the transcript does not show a clear voiced fix (فعلاً), so grammar-B low rather than grammar-A.

rows.why: 'I annoyed you' said with an extra -ti- (زعجتيك, the you-f ending) instead of I-past زعجتك; Amal recast زعجتك or أزعجتك. His أزعشتك at 15:02 is S4.
For 'you got annoyed with me' he reached for ما; she asked 'why ما?', he fixed to مني (16:10) and produced انزعجتي مني at 16:22 which she called Perfect.

Asking her to repeat بدك نشوف الواجب أو ناخد الفعل الجاي (16:33) he said كم مرة (how many times) for كمان مرة (sheet: one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة); she just rephrased the question (16:41); the same rendering recurs at 25:38 while ASR writes كمان correctly elsewhere (43:58, 57:03), so not an ASR drop.
rows.english: one more time? / say that again?
rows.r3_why: Real let-pass vocab slip, consistent across two moments; kept medium.

rows.why: Calque of 'one more' with أكتر; she supplied كمان واحد and he repeated it (sheet: some more / also / another | Kaman | كمان).
Addressing her (إنتي) the participle must be feminine; she prompted 'إنتي or انت?' and he fixed to مزعوجة (18:54).

rows.medi_said: And then باز is not بازوج, بازيجيني هدول اليوم.
rows.why: Subject is 'many things' (plural) so the verb needs the plural -و; he used singular; she recast بزعجوني and added بتزعجني is also fine but not بزعجني (20:18).
rows.english: Many things annoy me these days.

rows.why: Second attempt at the same sentence, again singular for a plural subject; she recast بزعجوني again and he then said بيزعجوني.
'These days' needs the plural أيام after هدول; he used singular اليوم; she supplied أيام and he said 'I even wrote أيام'.

rows.medi_said: أيام. I even wrote أيام. هدول أيام.
rows.why: The noun after هدول keeps its el-; his fixed version dropped it and she said طيب.

'Are you (f) sure' is the feminine participle متأكدة (sheet: sure / certain | Mit2akked | متأكد); he gave it a verb-like -ti ending; Amal only addressed اللي in this sentence (21:27-21:37); low because ASR may have mis-rendered the ending.
rows.r3_why: r1's piece is real and unflagged, kept low; r2's piece in this D (إلي→إنو) is the same row as D10 and is settled there - the pairing was a compare artefact.

rows.why: 'Sure THAT you didn't annoy him' takes the complementizer إنو; he used the relative اللي; Amal asked 'Why اللي؟' (21:27) then said 'إنو مش اللي' (21:35) and he said 'Oh, whoops'.
rows.english: (are you sure) that you (pl) didn't annoy him
rows.r3_why: Both readers actually found this row (r1-29 and r2-34); explicit fix in the transcript; high.

rows.why: The target sentence has an object 'him'; the -ه object ending is missing on the verb; she let it pass while fixing اللي.

rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: After إذا ما she keeps the b- (إذا ما بشوفك); he used the bare أشوفك; he repeated إذا ما بشوفك مبسوطة at 22:31 and asked about it; note her fix runs against the bucket text 'no b- after iza', but her form is the ruling; she also said no تكوني/بكون is needed before مبسوطة.
rows.english: I get annoyed if I don't see you happy.

rows.why: Target was the negative command 'don't be annoyed'; he gave the positive command; she prompted 'So don't be', he produced ما تنزعج then ما تنزعجي (23:32).
'With them' after annoyed is من + the -هم ending fused (منهم); transcript shows it split, possibly ASR spacing; she said بعدين and moved on.
After مش قصدهم ('they didn't mean to') the verb drops its b-; he kept it (بيدايقوكي); she recast يدايقوكي; he replied 'أنا بعرف هيك' keeping his form; the dropped ق is S4 and not counted.
rows.english: They didn't mean to upset you.

rows.why: Second occurrence: asked to repeat زي ما حكينا هديك المرة (25:29) he said كم مرة (how many times) for كمان مرة (sheet: one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة); she simply repeated زي ما حكينا and switched to English.
rows.english: one more time? / say that again?
rows.r3_why: Separate moment from D8 (not a duplicate), same let-pass slip; kept medium.

rows.medi_said: So I add his بزيء، بزياد،
rows.why: He fumbled the form of 'I add' as بزياد; Amal supplied بزيد.

rows.medi_said: and to remove his, uh, شول، فيل،
rows.why: Explaining the rule ('and to remove his...') he groped with non-words شول، فيل for a sheet word he had learned (i remove / take away | Ba2eem | بقيم) and did not ask; Amal supplied بقيم; he then said بعيم/بعين (dropped ق, S4, not scored); tier 1 as a non-word attempt at a known sheet word - not tier 2 (شول is not a form of بقيم) and not tier 0 (he attempted it, did not ask); low because the attempt is fragmentary.
rows.r3_why: Both saw it; transcript shows an attempt (not a question) at a sheet word she then supplied, so tier 1.

rows.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
rows.why: Idafa: the first word never takes el- (أول الفعل); he put el- on both, and answered her من وين? without the من; she said Mm.
rows.english: From the start of the verb, the start of the word.

rows.why: بخسر (I lose) said for بكسر (I break); she said 'close, بكسر'; he kept saying بخسر at 28:06, 28:18, 28:26 before switching to كسر; may be ruled S4 (ك/خ) but it is a different real word.
Past-tense ending must match هم; he gave the -t ending; she echoed it questioningly and he fixed to هم كسروا (28:47), which she confirmed.
Plain present needs the b- (بيكسروا); he dropped it for هم in the conjugation run; she said Nice and moved on.
'You (f) keep breaking' needs بتكسري with the bt- prefix; she said she did not hear the t and he then said بتكسري (33:31); his line is ASR-garbled.

rows.medi_said: Is it يسكر and يسكري؟ / يسكرو؟
rows.amal_said: The K is before the S.
rows.why: Root letters swapped (سكر = close/get drunk) for the command اكسر; he self-fixed at 34:20 but she still said the K comes before the S; his first shape also had a y- prefix instead of the command form; may be ruled S4.

rows.medi_said: Next far. Is it next far?
rows.amal_said: So it's either inكسر or انكسر.
rows.why: Asked for the past (ماضي, 36:38) of the in-verb بنكسر he offered a form ASR wrote as 'Next far' (most likely نكسر without the initial alef); Amal recast the past as انكسر (with the 'in-' onset) and he repeated انكسر at 37:05; low because his exact form is unrecoverable from the transcript.
rows.r3_why: He produced an Arabic verb form (not a meta question) and she recast it; real but his line is ASR garbage, so low.

rows.why: You-plural past in Levantine ends in -تو (كسرتوا as he said himself at 29:18), -تم is the MSA ending; she said طيب and moved on.
'His cups' needs the plural كاسات + -ه; he used the singular كاسته; she recast كاساته (transcript كساته); sheet: cup | Kaasa | كاسة.
For the singular 'his cup' she said كاسه twice (40:34, 40:46) against his كاسته; low because كاسته (kaasto) is also a common Levantine form and the transcript may be flattening her vowel.
كاسة is feminine so the verb takes -ت; he used masculine انكسر; she recast انكسرت, he asked why and worked out 'because it's female' (40:57).
كان agrees with عمر (masc), not with هي; he tried the feminine كانت; she said لأ، كان عمرها صح.
rows.english: when she was twelve (when her age was 12)

rows.why: The sentence was 'when she was 12'; he said eleven (إحداعش); she said 12, إتناش; he then said اثنعش (44:18); sheet: twelve | tna3sh | تنعش.
He added a feminine -ة to the term مضارع (present tense); she recast مضارع; he said المضارعة again at 44:41 and she let it pass.

rows.medi_said: Uh, هي بينكسو-- بينكسر. هو بينكسر.
rows.why: He gave the he-form بينكسر for هي; she said هو (that form is for he); he then produced هي بتنكسر (45:46) and she said حلو.
We-form of انكسر is بننكسر; his بنكسر is either 'we break' or 'I get broken'; her 45:57 line is garbled (بتنكسر) and she moved to a side note, so no clear signal.

rows.medi_said: conditioning, air conditionery. Do I say for air condition?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say 'my air conditioning' and she supplied the تبعي possessive with el- on the noun; he echoed it as تباين (48:31) which she let pass; neither 'air conditioning' nor تبع is on her sheet, so tier 0.
rows.r3_why: Clear asked/supplied exchange in the transcript; tier 0 didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: إن كسر من-- من الحرارة or
rows.amal_said: You would use انكسر، بس my, my issue is with the verb itself like كسر، مكسور، بكسر، بنكسر. It's physical.
rows.why: He used انكسر (physically broke) for the AC stopping working; she recast انكسر (49:31) then explained كسر is only physical and the right verb is خرب/خربان (48:49-50:09); he agreed and rewrote the sentence.
rows.english: It (the AC) broke from the heat.

rows.medi_said: بكسور-- بكسر، أنا ما بكسر، uh, اشي
rows.amal_said: بكسر أو كسرت؟ / لا، who said that? ... The only thing with أبداً is the consistent thing is ما.
rows.why: 'I have never broken anything' is past كسرت; he used present بكسر believing أبداً forces present; she asked بكسر أو كسرت؟, said لا, and he produced أنا أبدًا ما كسرت ولا اشي (52:44).

rows.amal_said: Tired me out. / Do you wanna say because the, the air conditioning tired me?
rows.why: He meant 'my AC' (تبعي, which she had given at 48:29) but said تعبي, which she heard as 'tired me' and asked about; he then dropped the word and said الـ air conditioning كان خربان (53:29).
rows.english: Because my air conditioning was broken.

rows.why: Negation goes on the verb with ما (ما نمت منيح), not مش on the adverb; she recast and he repeated ما نِمِت منيح (53:54).

rows.medi_said: إن و-- إن. الف-الفعلات. الفعلات إن.
rows.why: Invented plural فعلات for فعل (sheet: verb – verbs | Fe3el | فعل); she supplied the broken plural أفعال and he said الأفعال إن.

'I am annoyed' is the passive participle مزعوج; he gave the active مزعج (annoying); she said أنا مزعوج at the same moment he self-corrected, then checked he knew أنا مزعج = I'm annoying (56:52); sheet lists both annoyed | مزعوج and annoying | مزعج.

rows.medi_said: آخر فعل is... is it بزور بنكسر؟ بنكسر. أكسر. Okay.
rows.why: Naming the last verb pair he gave the bare أكسر for 'I break'; the plain present takes b- (بكسر); she recast بكسر and بنكسر.

Answering her يلا بشوفك (see you) he said ما شوفتك (I didn't see you): a negated past where the b-present بشوفك is needed; she just said باي; low because the ASR may have mis-heard a mumbled بشوفك / منشوفك.
rows.r3_why: Both saw it; the piece he needed is the b-present (B1), the form he used was a past (B5 as bucket2).
